rubric:
# Bilingual home-chooser review requirements

Read all 19 supplied surfaces, first as complete documents and genuine reading
units, then at each contextual-heading, independent-action and catalog-value
role. Judge the nine new Russian values directly against their supplied English
values. Check meaning, technical terminology, explicit actors and referents,
order, scope, prerequisites, accessible names and natural technical Russian.
Do not invent or narrow the requirements below. A contextual heading need not
repeat its associated card. The card paragraphs form a genuine reading group;
do not import unrelated material to rescue an independent action or catalog
value. A canonical-English ambiguity affecting these requirements is a source
blocker, not permission to repair the source in Russian.

Course purposes describe what the learner will study; they must not become
claims that later practical work or measured improvements have already been
completed. The practical course extends the completed Rust model, begins with
an orientation Chapter 0, and is available in English. Its prerequisite has
two alternatives: the first course's basics, or equivalent experience covering
both Rust and LLMs. The first course covers Chapters 0–39.

## Frozen per-surface requirements

| Surface ID | Required role and commitments |
| --- | --- |
| home.complete-document | Present a coherent course choice within the complete home page. The two named starts, their corresponding purposes and the practical course's prerequisite, English availability and orientation start must remain associated with the right course. Assess the nine new values and their coherence with preserved surrounding text; do not reopen unchanged lessons or certify all preserved translations. |
| home.selection.reading-unit | In actual order, present the selection heading, then the complete basics card, then the complete practical card. Distinguish the two purposes and two starts. Preserve the first course's Chapter 0–39 scope and local Chapter 0 destination; preserve the practical extension purpose, alternative prerequisite, English availability and Chapter 0 structure destination. |
| home.selection.heading | Name the section's course-selection operation and label its associated two-card section. Do not require this contextual heading to contain the cards' explanations. |
| home.basics.card-group | Associate the first course's name with building the components of a small language model in Rust, from tokenization through training and generation, Chapters 0–39, and its named start. Read its actual heading → description → action sequence together. |
| home.basics.heading | Identify the first course within its associated card. Do not require the heading to repeat its description or chapter range. |
| home.basics.start-action | Independently name starting the first course, distinguish it from the practical start, and preserve the Russian first-course Chapter 0 destination /ru/course/00-llm-parts/. |
| home.practical.card-group | Associate Practical LLM in Rust with extending the completed model through corpus preparation, efficient execution and measured training and inference. State starting at Chapter 0 about course structure, the two prerequisite alternatives, English availability and the named start. Read heading → description → prerequisite → language → action together; preserve /en/practical-llm-in-rust/00-course-structure/ and hreflang=en, without implying Russian practical lessons. |
| home.practical.heading | Identify the associated practical card with the exact product name Practical LLM in Rust. This product name is copied; the contextual heading need not repeat purpose or availability. |
| home.practical.start-action | Independently name starting Practical LLM in Rust, distinguish it from the basics action, and preserve /en/practical-llm-in-rust/00-course-structure/ with hreflang=en. The Russian action wording retains its inherited Russian language. |
| catalog.complete-document | Carry the complete target catalog, not a nine-field substitute. Its nine new chooser values must agree with their rendered roles and each other. The other 33 target values are preserved context; assess their fit to the new choice without newly certifying their language. The two practical-index fields are absent from this target catalog and this translation scope. |
| catalog.courseSelectionTitle | Supply the contextual section label naming the operation of choosing a course. |
| catalog.basicsCourseTitle | Supply the first course's name, matching its card and named start. |
| catalog.basicsCourseDescription | In its first-course description role, state building a small language model's components in Rust, from tokenization through training and generation, with Chapter 0–39 scope. |
| catalog.basicsCourseStart | Supply an independent action naming starting the first course; distinguish it from the practical action. |
| catalog.practicalCourseTitle | Supply the exact product name Practical LLM in Rust for its practical-card title role. |
| catalog.practicalCourseDescription | In its practical-course description role, state extending the completed model with corpus preparation, efficient execution, and measured training and inference; direct the learner to Chapter 0 explaining course structure. Preserve the learning-purpose scope. |
| catalog.practicalCoursePrerequisite | In its practical-course prerequisite role, state the basics of the first course or equivalent experience covering both Rust and LLMs. Do not turn an alternative into a cumulative requirement or require completion of every first-course chapter. |
| catalog.practicalCourseLanguage | In its practical-course availability role, clearly name English as the language in which that course is available. Do not imply translated practical lessons. |
| catalog.practicalCourseStart | Supply an independent action naming starting Practical LLM in Rust; distinguish it from the basics action. |

## Frozen catalog dispositions

The nine in-scope keys are courseSelectionTitle, basicsCourseTitle,
basicsCourseDescription, basicsCourseStart, practicalCourseTitle,
practicalCourseDescription, practicalCoursePrerequisite,
practicalCourseLanguage and practicalCourseStart. practicalCourseTitle is
copied as an exact product name; the other eight values are translated.

The 33 preserved context keys are siteTitle, siteDescription, skipToContent,
homeLabel, languageSwitchLabel, darkThemeLabel, languagePickerTitle,
languagePickerIntro, eyebrow, homeTitle, homeIntro, examplesTitle,
examplesDescription, formulasTitle, formulasDescription, historyTitle,
historyDescription, courseNote, courseLinkLabel, repositoryLinkLabel,
courseEyebrow, courseTitle, courseDescription, courseEmpty,
contentRevisionLabel, allChaptersLabel, chapterObjectiveLabel,
chapterNavigationLabel, previousChapterLabel, nextChapterLabel,
diagramFullViewOpenLabel, diagramFullViewCloseLabel and footerNote. They
are not copy classifications or new language approvals. The source-only
practicalCourseEyebrow and practicalIndexDescription belong to the practical
index and are absent from the Russian target; neither is a missing home
translation.

Complete-file provenance includes the actual catalogs and built home pages.
Check that the field dispositions fit those complete documents. Literal course
IDs, links, Rust, LLM and the practical product name retain their roles.

Report concrete changed meaning, terminology, grammar or accessibility
problems, with affected surface IDs, visible evidence, learner consequence and
a correction criterion. Do not demand a rewrite solely because another valid
wording is possible. Distinguish blocking defects from concrete nonblocking
advisories. Do not edit the candidate; a clean pass is acceptable.

surfaces.sourceText:
Skip to content
λ LLM, piece by piece
Language Русский

From text to a working model

Build an LLM from first principles

Follow small, executable examples until tensors, attention, training, and generation fit together as one Rust program.

Choose a course

LLM from scratch

Build the parts of a small language model in Rust, from tokenization to training and generation. Chapters 0–39.

Start LLM from scratch

Practical LLM in Rust

Extend the completed model with corpus preparation, efficient execution, and measured training and inference. Start with the course structure in Chapter 0.

Requires the basics from LLM from scratch or equivalent Rust and LLM experience.

Available in English

Start Practical LLM in Rust
01

Learn by running code

Every concept begins with a tiny Rust example and deterministic output.

02

Connect code to the formula

Symbols are introduced only when they explain the behavior you can observe.

03

See what came before

Each chapter contrasts the modern component with the historical approach it replaced.

⌁
Browse all examples on GitHub ↗

A static, localized course for understanding language models from the inside.
surfaces.targetText:
Перейти к содержимому
λ LLM по частям
Язык English

От текста к работающей модели

Создайте LLM с нуля

Начните с небольших запускаемых примеров и постепенно объедините тензоры, внимание, обучение и генерацию в одной программе на Rust.

Выберите курс

LLM с нуля

Реализуйте компоненты небольшой языковой модели на Rust: от токенизации до обучения и генерации. Главы 0–39.

Начать курс «LLM с нуля»

Practical LLM in Rust

Расширьте готовую модель: добавьте подготовку корпуса и эффективное выполнение вычислений, измеряйте результаты обучения и инференса. Начните с главы 0 об устройстве курса.

Нужно знать основы из курса «LLM с нуля» либо иметь сопоставимый опыт работы с Rust и LLM.

Курс доступен на английском языке

Начать курс Practical LLM in Rust
01

Учитесь, запуская код

Каждая тема начинается с небольшого примера на Rust, который можно запустить и получить воспроизводимый результат.

02

Сопоставляйте код с формулами

Обозначения вводятся только тогда, когда помогают объяснить результат, который можно увидеть в программе.

03

Узнайте, как задачу решали раньше

В каждой главе современный компонент сравнивается с предшествовавшим ему подходом.

⌁
Посмотреть все примеры на GitHub ↗

Статический курс о внутреннем устройстве языковых моделей, доступный на нескольких языках.
